question: Should OpenClaw add a core child-visible pre-timeout warning/grace contract for sub-agent runs, and what config/tool surface and native/ACP delivery semantics should it use?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but the fix adds public config/API behavior and cross-runtime lifecycle semantics that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define core warning contract
options.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, decide whether per-spawn overrides are allowed, and implement warning delivery for native and ACP runs with lifecycle tests.

options.title: Improve post-timeout recovery instead
options.body: Decline pre-timeout child warnings for now and route the lost-work pain to parent notification, durable completion delivery, and recovery issues.

options.title: Document checkpoint prompting only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document prompt-level checkpointing guidance rather than adding new config or control messages.

recommendation.title: Define core warning contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, decide whether per-spawn overrides are allowed, and implement warning delivery for native and ACP runs with lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on the subagent lifecycle/config boundary and posted prior maintainer-side review context for this item.
